subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Adapted and Lifelong Inclusive Activity Design
title: Guided practice A: adapted sport and inclusive formats as durable options
focus: adapted sport and inclusive formats as durable options
essentialQuestion: How does an activity have to change to still be there at forty, or after an injury?
privacySafeScenario: Take one activity the learner values and produce three adapted versions of it — for reduced mobility, for very limited time, and for a mixed-age group — with the reasoning for each.
studentTask: Learner applies adapted sport and inclusive formats as durable options in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind adapted sport and inclusive formats as durable options and name one adjustment for the next session.
completionCriteria: The learner completes or fully describes the adapted sport and inclusive formats as durable options task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
adaptationChoices: Adaptations may be written, diagrammed, described aloud, or trialed practically; practical trial is optional.
extensionChallenge: Apply adapted sport and inclusive formats as durable options under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Adaptations may be written, diagrammed, described aloud, or trialed practically; practical trial is optional.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of adapted sport and inclusive formats as durable options in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
